page: Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv5 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The instance features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 32.0 GB of memory per core. The hardware configuration also includes 2458 GB of local SSD storage, and it runs under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations place the E64-16ds_v5 in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks, with a few notable exceptions. The system achieved a PassMark memory score of 2827.67, which is classified as strong (top 25%). Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks show read speeds of 103.1 GB/sec and write speeds of 59.48 GB/sec. CPU performance is stable, with a PassMark CPU score of 21387.42 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10172.0. In database operations, the server processed 15.93 million Redis SET operations per second and scored 8079.86 on PassMark database tests.

The qualitative cost profile of this instance reflects its high memory-to-vCPU ratio. By bundling 512.0 GB of RAM with only 16 vCPUs, it offers a cost-efficient alternative for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU processing. This design prevents over-provisioning compute resources just to acquire necessary memory capacity. However, the tradeoff is a lower multi-core compute ceiling relative to the massive memory pool. This configuration is designed for large in-memory databases, caching layers, data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
